Conceptual connection: a selected antibody-producing cell lineage supplies the specificity retained by a hybridoma.
Conceptual connection: cultured cells can preserve and propagate a useful biological property—in this case, antibody production.
Conceptual connection: population-level transmission questions are expressed as changes among susceptible, infectious, and removed groups.
Conceptual connection: coupled rate equations connect infection and removal with depletion of susceptible individuals.
Evidence-based practice appraises clinical trials when appropriate; different clinical questions can require other study designs.
Conceptual connection: comparing populations and assessing bias underpin critical appraisal of clinical evidence.
Nowell applied heritable variation and selection to competing tumor-cell populations.
Conceptual connection: variants can exist before treatment selects among them, clarifying one route to changing tumor behavior.
The 1996 CTLA-4 experiments used antibody blockade to test whether releasing an inhibitory signal enhanced antitumor responses.
Conceptual connection: checkpoint therapies modify inhibitory regulation of adaptive immune responses to tumors.
Conceptual connection: layered rocks preserve evidence of deposition and later transformation, allowing reconstruction of crustal recycling.
Conceptual connection: repeated erosion, burial, and uplift require an Earth history extending far beyond human records.
Conceptual connection: earthquake observations and measured deformation supply the event-scale evidence that elastic rebound explains.
Conceptual connection: stored elastic strain and its release provide a mechanical account of fault displacement and seismic energy.
Holmes proposed subcrustal convection as a mechanism capable of helping explain continental movement.
Conceptual connection: radioactive heat supplied an internal-energy source relevant to Holmes’s convection argument.
Conceptual connection: motion-induced electric currents and magnetic feedback supply the physical principle of a self-sustaining fluid dynamo.
Conceptual connection: groundwater storage and movement become quantitative parts of hydrology through a flow–gradient relationship.
Conceptual connection: pressure contributes to hydraulic head, whose gradient drives flow through porous material.
Conceptual connection: rotating-frame mechanics and friction permit a mathematical balance for wind-driven ocean motion.
Conceptual connection: observed current directions become a specific explanation of wind forcing in a rotating ocean.
Conceptual connection: wind-driven rotating-ocean theory is extended from local vertical transport to circulation constrained by a basin.
Conceptual connection: spatial flow equations represent how wind, friction, and latitude-dependent rotation create an asymmetric gyre.
Conceptual connection: circulation driven by density contrasts becomes a feedback problem when transport itself changes temperature and salinity.
Conceptual connection: coupled reservoir balances allow multiple circulation equilibria to be derived under explicit idealizations.
Conceptual connection: equatorial ocean-temperature changes and currents participate in the coupled Pacific feedback described by Bjerknes.
Conceptual connection: representing interactions between climate components makes ocean–atmosphere feedback explicit; this is not a claimed transmission from one model.
Conceptual connection: changing ice coverage raises the energy-balance question of how reflected sunlight amplifies climatic shifts.
Conceptual connection: energy-balance modeling allows temperature-dependent reflectivity to be included as a climate feedback.
Conceptual connection: marine isotope records provide an independent archive for investigating repeated glacial and interglacial conditions.
Conceptual connection: sedimentary sequence places isotope measurements into an ordered record of environmental change.
Conceptual connection: hydrogen-ion concentration and acid–base equilibria explain why added carbon dioxide changes seawater pH.
Conceptual connection: uptake of anthropogenic carbon links the atmospheric carbon cycle to changes in marine carbonate chemistry.
Conceptual connection: coupled carbon-cycle calculations extend emissions scenarios into long-term projections of ocean chemistry.
